title: Clienti e vicini
subtitle: Customers and neighbours
intro: Opening week. A German tourist with a flat tyre, a nonna who wants a bike for her grandson, Pasquale who complains about the sign, the comune that wants a form for the sign, and a first real complaint. Everyone is polite, and politeness in Italian runs on the condizionale: vorrei, potrebbe, dovreste. This unit adds the conditional, the formal imperative in practice, ne, the combined pronouns (glielo, me la, ce ne) and the relative pronouns che and cui.
objectives: Ask, suggest and refuse politely: [[vorrei una camera d'aria]], [[potrebbe ripararla oggi?]], [[dovreste rifare il cartello]], [[non potrei, mi dispiace]]
Use the formal imperative with customers: [[mi dica]], [[si accomodi]], [[non si preoccupi]], [[torni domani]]
Use ne for quantities and "about it": [[ne vorrei due]], [[quante ne ha?]], [[ne parliamo domani]]
Combine two pronouns: [[glielo ordino]], [[me la cambia?]], [[ce ne sono tre]], [[te lo prometto]]
Describe with che and cui: [[la bici che ha comprato]], [[il cliente di cui ti parlavo]], [[il giorno in cui abbiamo aperto]]
canDo: A2 · Spoken interaction: can deal with common situations in a shop (requests, prices, repairs, exchanges) and make a simple complaint politely.
A2 · Spoken interaction: can make suggestions and give advice, agree and disagree politely.
A2 · Spoken production: can express an opinion and give a simple reason.
A2 · Listening: can understand a polite request or complaint and the reply.
A2 · Writing: can write a short polite message to request, apologise or complain.

sections.title: La prima settimana
sections.intro: Tuesday with the customers, Friday with the neighbours. Listen for vorrei, potrebbe, dovreste; for mi dica, si accomodi, non si preoccupi; for ne and for glielo, me la, ce ne.

blocks.title: Una gomma e una bici per un nipote
blocks.setting: Martedì, ore 10. Ciclofficina Ferrante, via Marina. Fuori, una bici da viaggio tedesca con la ruota posteriore a terra e un signore con i sandali. Dentro, dieci minuti dopo, una signora con una borsa della spesa e un'idea chiara.

lines.t: Buongiorno. Ho una gomma a terra. Potrebbe ripararla oggi? Domani vorrei andare a Otranto.
lines.n: Good morning. I have a flat tyre. Could you repair it today? Tomorrow I'd like to go to Otranto.
lines.note: Potrebbe: could you (formal). Vorrei: I'd like. The conditional of politeness, in a tourist's careful Italian.

lines.t: Certo. Mi faccia vedere. È la camera d'aria: l'ha bucata su un chiodo. Gliela cambio subito, dieci minuti. Ne ho una della sua misura.
lines.n: Of course. Let me see. It's the inner tube: you punctured it on a nail. I'll change it for you right away, ten minutes. I have one in your size.
lines.note: Mi faccia vedere: Lei imperative with mi before it. Gliela cambio: glie + la = to you (formal) + it. Ne ho una: I have one of them.

lines.t: Quanto verrebbe?
lines.n: How much would it come to?
lines.note: Verrebbe: the conditional of venire, for a price not yet fixed.

lines.t: Dodici euro con la camera d'aria. Si accomodi, c'è una sedia fuori. Vuole un caffè? Nando lo porta.
lines.n: Twelve euros with the inner tube. Take a seat, there's a chair outside. Do you want a coffee? Nando brings it.
lines.note: Si accomodi: the formal invitation to sit. Nando's bar delivers to the shop, which is the business model.

lines.t: Volentieri. Lei è di qui? Parla come un canadese.
lines.n: Gladly. Are you from here? You talk like a Canadian.
lines.note: Even the German hears it.

lines.stage: Ten minutes later. Klaus leaves with a coffee inside him and a working tyre. The woman with the shopping bag has been waiting at the door, not patiently.

lines.t: Buongiorno. Sono la signora Rizzo, la mamma di Franca, la farmacista. Vorrei una bici per mio nipote, che ha otto anni e che non sta mai fermo.
lines.n: Good morning. I'm Mrs Rizzo, Franca the pharmacist's mother. I'd like a bike for my grandson, who is eight and who never keeps still.
lines.note: Che ha otto anni: the relative che, for people and things, subject or object. Every customer in Roccamarina is somebody's relative.

lines.t: Mi dica, signora. Quanto è alto, più o meno?
lines.n: Tell me, madam. How tall is he, roughly?

lines.t: Così. Avrei bisogno di una bici che duri. L'ultima, quella che gli ha comprato suo padre al supermercato, si è rotta in un mese.
lines.n: Like this. I'd need a bike that lasts. The last one, the one his father bought him at the supermarket, broke in a month.
lines.note: Avrei bisogno di: I'd need, softer than ho bisogno. Una bici che duri: che + subjunctive for a quality wanted, unit 16; recognise. Quella che gli ha comprato: the one that he bought him.

lines.t: Ne ho due da bambino, ma sono usate. Una nuova gliela potrei ordinare: arriverebbe in una settimana e costerebbe sui centottanta euro.
lines.n: I have two children's bikes, but they're second-hand. A new one I could order for you: it would arrive in a week and would cost around a hundred and eighty euros.
lines.note: Ne ho due: I have two of them. Gliela potrei ordinare: to you + it + could order. Arriverebbe, costerebbe: conditionals for what would happen.

lines.t: Centottanta! Per un bambino di otto anni che la romperà in un mese? Non potrei spendere meno?
lines.n: A hundred and eighty! For an eight-year-old who'll break it in a month? Couldn't I spend less?
lines.note: Non potrei…? Couldn't I…? The polite negotiation.

lines.t: Le usate costano sessanta, e gliele sistemo come nuove. Se poi la rompe, me la riporta e gliela riparo gratis per un anno. Che ne dice?
lines.n: The second-hand ones cost sixty, and I'll fix them up like new for you. If he breaks it, you bring it back to me and I'll repair it free for a year. What do you say?
lines.note: Gliele sistemo: to you + them. Me la riporta: to me + it. Che ne dice? What do you say (about it)?

lines.t: Dico che mi prende la rossa. E che lo dirò a Franca.
lines.n: I say I'll take the red one. And that I'll tell Franca.
lines.note: Mi prende la rossa: literally "you take me the red one", the ethical mi of southern Italian: I'll have the red one.

notes.phrase: vorrei · potrebbe · avrei bisogno · non potrei · verrebbe · costerebbe
notes.note: The condizionale: requests, prices, hypotheses, all one tense. Softer than the present in every case.

notes.phrase: mi faccia vedere · si accomodi · mi dica
notes.note: Lei imperatives with their pronouns in front. The shopkeeper's three essentials.

notes.phrase: ne ho una · ne ho due · che ne dice?
notes.note: Ne = of them, of it. Replaces a quantity or a di-phrase.

notes.phrase: gliela cambio · gliela potrei ordinare · gliele sistemo · me la riporta
notes.note: Two pronouns together: indirect + direct. Gli / le → glie-, mi → me, before lo, la, li, le, ne.

blocks.title: Il cartello, il comune, il reclamo
blocks.setting: Venerdì. Prima Pasquale sulla soglia, poi l'ufficio SUAP del comune (Antonella Moro, stessa pianta), poi Klaus di nuovo, meno contento.
blocks.register: informale con Pasquale, formale con Antonella e Klaus

lines.t: Quel cartello. «Bici & Mare» con la e commerciale. In italiano si scrive «e». E la A di Ferrante è storta.
lines.n: That sign. «Bici & Mare» with the ampersand. In Italian you write «e». And the A in Ferrante is crooked.
lines.note: La e commerciale: the ampersand. Pasquale's first visit is a complaint, which for him is a greeting.

lines.t: Pasquale, la A l'ha dipinta Tommaso. Glielo dico io, così la rifà. Vorresti entrare o preferiresti criticare da fuori?
lines.n: Pasquale, Tommaso painted the A. I'll tell him, so he redoes it. Would you like to come in or would you prefer to criticise from outside?
lines.note: Glielo dico: to him + it. Vorresti, preferiresti: tu conditionals, with irony.

lines.t: Entrerei, ma dovreste anche sapere che per quel cartello vi serve un permesso. Occupazione di suolo pubblico. Ve lo dico da amico.
lines.n: I'd come in, but you should also know that for that sign you need a permit. Occupation of public land. I'm telling you as a friend.
lines.note: Entrerei, dovreste: more conditionals. Ve lo dico: to you (pl.) + it.

lines.stage: The SUAP desk at the comune, an hour later. Antonella Moro has a new plant and the same expression.

lines.t: Buongiorno. Mi dica.
lines.n: Good morning. How can I help?

lines.t: Buongiorno, dottoressa. Avrei una domanda sul cartello dell'officina in via Marina. Un vicino mi ha detto che servirebbe un permesso.
lines.n: Good morning, dottoressa. I'd have a question about the sign of the workshop in via Marina. A neighbour told me a permit would be needed.
lines.note: Avrei una domanda: I'd have a question, the polite opening. Servirebbe: would be needed.

lines.t: Il vicino sarebbe il professor Leone? Ha ragione, come sempre. Le servirebbe l'autorizzazione per l'insegna e, se il cartello sta sul marciapiede, anche l'occupazione di suolo pubblico. Compili questo e me lo riporti con due marche da bollo.
lines.n: Would the neighbour be Professor Leone? He's right, as always. You'd need the authorisation for the sign and, if the board stands on the pavement, the occupation of public land too. Fill this in and bring it back to me with two revenue stamps.
lines.note: Sarebbe: would be, for a guess. Compili, me lo riporti: Lei imperatives, the second with two pronouns in front.

lines.t: Due marche. Certo. Potrei portarglielo lunedì?
lines.n: Two stamps. Of course. Could I bring it to you on Monday?
lines.note: Portarglielo: bring + to you + it, all attached to the infinitive.

lines.t: Lunedì va bene. E tolga il cartello dal marciapiede finché non ha il permesso: i vigili passano il sabato. Non si preoccupi, è una pratica semplice. Dieci giorni.
lines.n: Monday is fine. And take the board off the pavement until you have the permit: the municipal police come round on Saturdays. Don't worry, it's a simple procedure. Ten days.
lines.note: Tolga: Lei imperative of togliere. Non si preoccupi: don't worry (formal). Dieci giorni: in Antonella's calendar.

lines.stage: 4 p.m. Klaus is back. The rear tyre is flat again. He is not smiling, but he is polite, which is worse.

lines.t: Mi scusi, ma avrei un problema. La gomma che mi ha cambiato stamattina è di nuovo a terra. Sono arrivato a Torre dell'Orso e sono tornato a piedi.
lines.n: Excuse me, but I'd have a problem. The tyre you changed for me this morning is flat again. I got to Torre dell'Orso and walked back.
lines.note: Mi scusi, ma avrei un problema: the perfect Italian complaint. Conditional, mi scusi, ma. La gomma che mi ha cambiato: the relative che as object.

lines.t: Ha ragione, mi dispiace. È colpa mia: non ho controllato il copertone, e il chiodo era ancora dentro. Gliela rifaccio adesso, e stavolta cambio anche il copertone. Non le faccio pagare niente, né stamattina né ora.
lines.n: You're right, I'm sorry. It's my fault: I didn't check the outer tyre, and the nail was still in it. I'll redo it for you now, and this time I'll change the outer tyre too. I won't charge you anything, neither this morning nor now.
lines.note: Ha ragione, mi dispiace, è colpa mia: the three sentences of an apology. Non le faccio pagare: I won't make you pay.

lines.t: Non sarebbe necessario. Ma accetto. E domani, Otranto?
lines.n: That wouldn't be necessary. But I accept. And tomorrow, Otranto?
lines.note: Non sarebbe necessario: the polite refusal of the refund, followed by accepting it.

lines.t: Domani Otranto. Con un copertone nuovo di cui mi fido. E un caffè, di cui si fida Nando.
lines.n: Tomorrow Otranto. With a new tyre I trust. And a coffee, which Nando trusts.
lines.note: Di cui mi fido: fidarsi di → di cui. Cui after a preposition, for people and things.

notes.phrase: Avrei una domanda. · Avrei un problema. · Mi scusi, ma… · Non sarebbe necessario.
notes.note: The conditional softens both the request and the complaint. Italians complain in the conditional and refuse in it too.

notes.phrase: compili · me lo riporti · tolga · non si preoccupi
notes.note: Lei imperatives, with the pronouns before the verb (me lo riporti) and non before the negative.

notes.phrase: glielo dico · ve lo dico · portarglielo · gliela rifaccio
notes.note: Combined pronouns, before the verb or attached to the infinitive as one word.

notes.phrase: la gomma che mi ha cambiato · un copertone di cui mi fido · il vicino di cui parlavo
notes.note: Che without a preposition; cui after one (di cui, a cui, con cui, in cui).

questions.q: The protagonist charges Klaus for the second repair.
questions.t: Non le faccio pagare niente, né stamattina né ora.
questions.why: Neither repair is charged: it was the shop's fault, and the nail was still in the tyre.

questions.q: What does Antonella say the shop needs?
options: An authorisation for the sign and, for the board on the pavement, the occupation of public land.
A new sign in Italian without the ampersand.
questions.why: L'autorizzazione per l'insegna e l'occupazione di suolo pubblico. Pasquale, as always, was right.

questions.q: ___ (io, volere) una camera d'aria. ___ (Lei, potere) ripararla oggi? ___ (costare) dodici euro.
questions.n: I'd like an inner tube. Could you repair it today? It would cost twelve euros.

sections.title: Servizio, riparazioni, reclami
sections.intro: The words of serving a customer, of repairs and problems, of opinions, and of complaining and apologising with grace.

items.n: to serve (a customer); to be needed

ex.t: La servo subito, signora. Le serve altro?
ex.n: I'll serve you right away, madam. Do you need anything else?

items.note: Servire qualcuno: to serve someone (direct). Servire a qualcuno: to be needed by someone (unit 13).

items.n: receipt

ex.t: Ecco lo scontrino. Lo conservi per la garanzia.
ex.n: Here's the receipt. Keep it for the warranty.

items.note: Ricevuta: a receipt for a service; fattura: an invoice. By law the shop must give one.

items.n: warranty, guarantee

ex.t: Due anni di garanzia sulle bici nuove, un anno sulle usate.
ex.n: Two years' warranty on new bikes, one year on second-hand ones.

items.note: In garanzia: under warranty. EU law: two years on new goods.

items.n: discount

ex.t: Mi farebbe uno sconto? — Il dieci per cento, perché è la mamma di Franca.
ex.n: Would you give me a discount? — Ten percent, because you're Franca's mother.

items.note: Fare uno sconto: to give a discount. Scontato: discounted. Saldi: sales.

items.n: second-hand, used

ex.t: Le bici usate costano sessanta euro.
ex.n: Second-hand bikes cost sixty euros.

items.note: L'usato: second-hand goods. Di seconda mano: same.

items.n: to order

ex.t: Gliela posso ordinare: arriva in una settimana.
ex.n: I can order it for you: it arrives in a week.

items.note: Also to order food and to tidy up. L'ordine: the order.

items.n: delivery

ex.t: Consegna in una settimana. Consegna a domicilio gratis in paese.
ex.n: Delivery in a week. Free home delivery in town.

items.note: Consegnare: to deliver, to hand over.

items.n: trust

ex.t: In paese si lavora sulla fiducia: paghi la prossima volta.
ex.n: In the village you work on trust: you pay next time.

items.note: Fidarsi di: to trust (reflexive, with di). Di fiducia: trusted (il meccanico di fiducia).

items.n: to note down; to put on the tab

ex.t: Non ho contanti. — Segno. Paghi la prossima volta.
ex.n: I don't have cash. — I'll put it on the tab. Pay next time.

items.note: Segnare also = to score (a goal) and to mark. The tab is the quaderno behind the counter.

items.n: gladly, with pleasure

ex.t: Vuole un caffè? — Volentieri.
ex.n: Do you want a coffee? — Gladly.

items.note: The yes of good manners. Also: lo farei volentieri, ma… (I'd gladly, but…).

items.n: size, measurement

ex.t: Ne ho una della sua misura. Che misura porta?
ex.n: I have one in your size. What size do you take?

items.note: Taglia for clothes, numero for shoes, misura for everything else.

items.n: inner tube

ex.t: È la camera d'aria: l'ha bucata su un chiodo.
ex.n: It's the inner tube: you punctured it on a nail.

items.note: Copertone: the outer tyre. Gomma: either, informally.

items.n: to puncture

ex.t: Ho bucato. Ho bucato due volte in un giorno.
ex.n: I got a puncture. I got two punctures in one day.

items.note: Bucare alone = to get a puncture. Il buco: the hole. Forare: same, more formal.

items.n: nail

ex.t: Il chiodo era ancora dentro al copertone.
ex.n: The nail was still in the tyre.

items.note: Also a stud and, in slang, a debt. Vite: screw.

items.n: breakdown, fault; broken

ex.t: Un guasto al cambio. Il cambio è guasto.
ex.n: A fault in the gears. The gears are broken.

items.note: Noun and adjective. Guasto for machines; rotto for things that break.

items.n: to work (a machine)

ex.t: I freni non funzionano. Adesso funziona.
ex.n: The brakes don't work. Now it works.

items.note: Machines funzionano; people lavorano. Non funziona: it doesn't work.

items.n: to check

ex.t: Non ho controllato il copertone. Controlli i freni ogni mese.
ex.n: I didn't check the outer tyre. Check the brakes every month.

items.note: Il controllo: the check. Also to control.

items.n: to replace

ex.t: Sostituisco la camera d'aria e il copertone.
ex.n: I'll replace the inner tube and the outer tyre.

items.note: -isc- verb. La sostituzione: the replacement. Pezzo di ricambio: spare part.

items.n: to adjust; regular

ex.t: Le regolo i freni e la sella. Manutenzione regolare.
ex.n: I'll adjust your brakes and saddle. Regular maintenance.

items.note: Verb and adjective. La regolazione: the adjustment.

items.n: defect, flaw

ex.t: È un difetto di fabbrica: è in garanzia.
ex.n: It's a factory defect: it's under warranty.

items.note: Difettoso: faulty. Also a character flaw.

items.n: to fix up, to sort out

ex.t: Gliele sistemo come nuove. Sistemo tutto io.
ex.n: I'll fix them up like new for you. I'll sort everything out.

items.note: The all-purpose southern verb: to fix, tidy, arrange, settle. Sistemarsi: to settle down.

items.n: free of charge

ex.t: Gliela riparo gratis per un anno.
ex.n: I'll repair it for you free for a year.

items.note: Invariable. Gratuito: the adjective. Non le faccio pagare niente: I won't charge you.

items.n: complaint

ex.t: Il primo reclamo della settimana: una gomma a terra due volte.
ex.n: The first complaint of the week: a flat tyre twice.

items.note: Fare un reclamo: to complain formally. Lamentela: a grumble.

items.n: to complain

ex.t: Pasquale si lamenta del cartello. Si lamenta sempre di qualcosa.
ex.n: Pasquale complains about the sign. He always complains about something.

items.note: Lamentarsi di + thing, con + person. Reflexive, essere in the past.

items.n: to apologise

ex.t: Mi sono scusato con il cliente. Chiedo scusa.
ex.n: I apologised to the customer. I apologise.

items.note: Scusarsi con qualcuno di / per qualcosa. Chiedere scusa: to say sorry. Le scuse: the apologies.

items.n: fault, blame

ex.t: È colpa mia. Non è colpa sua. Di chi è la colpa?
ex.n: It's my fault. It's not your fault. Whose fault is it?

items.note: Colpa mia, colpa tua: no article. Dare la colpa a: to blame.

items.n: to be right

ex.t: Ha ragione, mi dispiace. Pasquale ha sempre ragione.
ex.n: You're right, I'm sorry. Pasquale is always right.

items.note: Avere torto: to be wrong. Not essere.

items.n: to put right, to make up for

ex.t: Rimedio subito: gliela rifaccio e non paga.
ex.n: I'll put it right straight away: I'll redo it and you don't pay.

items.note: Rimediare a + the problem. Un rimedio: a remedy.

items.n: refund

ex.t: Vuole il rimborso o la sostituzione?
ex.n: Do you want a refund or a replacement?

items.note: Rimborsare: to refund. Rarer than in Canada: the Italian default is the replacement.

items.n: don't worry (formal)

ex.t: Non si preoccupi, è una pratica semplice. Non ti preoccupare, Tommaso.
ex.n: Don't worry, it's a simple procedure. Don't worry, Tommaso.

items.note: Lei: non si preoccupi. Tu: non ti preoccupare / non preoccuparti.

items.n: opinion

ex.t: Secondo me il cartello va bene. Pasquale ha un'altra opinione.
ex.n: In my opinion the sign is fine. Pasquale has another opinion.

items.note: Secondo me / te / lei: in my / your / her opinion. A mio parere: more formal.

items.n: to agree

ex.t: Sono d'accordo con Dora. Non sono d'accordo.
ex.n: I agree with Dora. I don't agree.

items.note: D'accordo! = OK, agreed. Essere d'accordo con + person, su + thing.

items.n: to advise, to recommend

ex.t: Le consiglierei la rossa. Ti consiglio di controllare i freni.
ex.n: I'd recommend the red one. I advise you to check the brakes.

items.note: Consigliare a qualcuno di + infinitive. Un consiglio: a piece of advice.

items.n: permit; permission

ex.t: Per il cartello serve un permesso. Permesso? — Avanti!
ex.n: For the sign you need a permit. May I come in? — Come in!

items.note: Permesso? is what you say at a door. Autorizzazione: authorisation, the official word.

items.n: public land (pavement, square)

ex.t: Occupazione di suolo pubblico: il cartello sul marciapiede si paga.
ex.n: Occupation of public land: a board on the pavement is paid for.

items.note: Tables outside a bar, a sign, a stall: all suolo pubblico, all taxed.

items.n: municipal police officer

ex.t: I vigili passano il sabato e fanno le multe.
ex.n: The municipal police come round on Saturdays and hand out fines.

items.note: Vigili urbani / polizia municipale: parking, signs, noise, markets. Not the carabinieri.

items.n: fine

ex.t: Cento euro di multa per un cartello senza permesso.
ex.n: A hundred-euro fine for a sign without a permit.

items.note: Fare / prendere una multa: to give / get a fine.

items.n: noise

ex.t: I vicini si lamentano del rumore dopo le dieci.
ex.n: The neighbours complain about the noise after ten.

items.note: Fare rumore: to make noise. Rumoroso: noisy.

sections.title: Vorrei, potrebbe, glielo, di cui
sections.intro: Five pieces: the conditional and what it is for, the formal imperative in use, ne, the combined pronouns, and che and cui. Reference pages at the end of each block.

blocks.title: Condizionale presente: vorrei, potrebbe, sarebbe
blocks.rule: Same stem as the future (parler-, prender-, sar-, avr-, vorr-, potr-, dovr-, far-) + -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero. Uses: polite requests and offers (vorrei, potrebbe, le dispiacerebbe), wishes (mi piacerebbe), advice (dovresti), hypotheses and prices (costerebbe, arriverebbe), opinions softened (direi, sarebbe meglio), unconfirmed news (il sindaco sarebbe…). The conditional never asks for a condition to be stated; it just softens.

blocks.caption: [[volere|to want]], [[potere|to be able to]], [[essere|to be]] · condizionale presente
blocks.note: The three you use most: vorrei, potrei / potrebbe, sarei / sarebbe. Dovere gives dovrei / dovrebbe.

head: Use
Italian
English
rows: Vorrei una camera d'aria. Potrebbe ripararla oggi? Le dispiacerebbe aspettare?
I'd like an inner tube. Could you repair it today? Would you mind waiting?
Le farei uno sconto. Gliela potrei ordinare.
I'd give you a discount. I could order it for you.
Mi piacerebbe vedere Otranto. Vorrei restare.
I'd like to see Otranto. I'd like to stay.
Dovresti controllare i freni. Dovreste rifare la A.
You should check the brakes. You should redo the A.
Costerebbe centottanta. Arriverebbe in una settimana. Quanto verrebbe?
It would cost 180. It would arrive in a week. How much would it come to?
Direi di sì. Sarebbe meglio aspettare. Non saprei.
I'd say yes. It would be better to wait. I wouldn't know.
Non potrei, mi dispiace. Non sarebbe necessario.
I couldn't, I'm sorry. That wouldn't be necessary.
Il sindaco sarebbe contrario. Il vicino sarebbe Pasquale.
The mayor is said to be against it. The neighbour would be Pasquale, I take it.

items.t: Avrei una domanda. Avrei bisogno di una bici che duri. Non potrei spendere meno?
items.n: I'd have a question. I'd need a bike that lasts. Couldn't I spend less?

items.t: Vorresti entrare o preferiresti criticare da fuori? — Entrerei, ma dovreste sapere una cosa.
items.n: Would you like to come in or would you rather criticise from outside? — I'd come in, but you should know one thing.

items.t: Sarebbe meglio togliere il cartello. I vigili potrebbero passare sabato.
items.n: It would be better to take the board away. The municipal police might come by on Saturday.

items.t: Mi piacerebbe andare a Otranto domani. Ci andrei in bici, se la gomma tenesse.
items.n: I'd like to go to Otranto tomorrow. I'd go by bike, if the tyre held.
items.note: se tenesse: congiuntivo imperfetto, unit 20

blocks.title: Would, could, should: one tense
blocks.text: English spreads it over three modals; Italian has one ending set. [[Vorrei]] = I would like, [[potrei]] = I could, [[dovrei]] = I should, [[sarebbe]] = it would be, [[farei]] = I would do. The present is for facts; the conditional is for everything you would rather not state as a fact: a request, a price, a piece of advice, a refusal. Shopkeepers live in it.

blocks.title: The formal imperative with customers
blocks.rule: Lei imperative: -are verbs take -i (guardi, compili, torni), -ere and -ire take -a (prenda, senta, tolga, finisca); irregular: sia, abbia, vada, faccia, dia, dica, stia, venga, esca, tenga, scelga. Pronouns go before it (mi dica, si accomodi, me lo riporti, non si preoccupi). Negative: non + the same form. The Loro form (-ino / -ano: si accomodino, prendano) is for a formal plural; recognise it, use voi.

blocks.title: ne: of it, of them, about it
blocks.rule: Ne replaces a noun after a quantity (ne ho due, ne vorrei un chilo, quante ne ha?, non ne ho) and a phrase with di (ne parliamo = we talk about it; che ne dici? = what do you say about it?; ne ho bisogno = I need it; me ne vado = I'm off). It goes before the verb or attaches to infinitives and imperatives (prendine una). In the passato prossimo the participle agrees with the quantity: ne ho comprate due.

blocks.title: Combined pronouns: glielo, me la, ce ne
blocks.rule: Indirect + direct pronoun together: the indirect comes first and changes its vowel to e (mi → me, ti → te, ci → ce, vi → ve); gli and le both become glie- and join the direct pronoun in one word (glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele, gliene). Then lo, la, li, le or ne. They go before the conjugated verb or attach to infinitives and tu / noi / voi imperatives as one word (portarglielo, dammelo). The participle agrees with the direct pronoun (gliel'ho data).

blocks.title: Relative pronouns: che and cui
blocks.rule: Che joins a noun to a clause that describes it, for people and things, as subject or direct object, never after a preposition: la gomma che ha bucato, il cliente che aspetta. Cui is used after a preposition (di cui, a cui, con cui, in cui, per cui, su cui, da cui): il cliente di cui parlavo, la bici a cui tengo, il giorno in cui abbiamo aperto. Il / la / i / le cui = whose. Chi = the person who (nobody in particular). Quello che / ciò che = what.

sections.title: Glielo, gliene: gli before a vowel, and the melody of a polite request
sections.intro: Two things this unit asks of your mouth: the gl + vowel of the combined pronouns (glielo, gliela, gliene), where the gli is one soft sound, and the rising, falling melody of a request in the conditional, which is where Italian politeness actually lives.

items.n: it to him / her / you
items.tip: Gli is the /ʎ/ of unit 4 (like the lli in million), and the following e is just a vowel: ʎe-lo, two syllables, stress on the first. Not gli-e-lo in three.

items.n: some of it to him / her / you
items.tip: Same: ʎe-ne. Gliene ordino una: ʎe-ne-OR-di-no. The whole cluster is one quick beat before the verb.

items.n: Could you repair it today?
items.tip: A conditional question rises on the last word and stresses the modal: po-TREB-be ri-pa-RAR-la OG-gi↗. The rise is the politeness; a flat version sounds like an order.

items.n: I couldn't, I'm sorry.
items.tip: The polite no falls gently and is followed by mi dispiace, falling again. Two falls, no pause: non po-TREI, mi di-SPIA-ce↘.

pairs.tip: The i is silent; gl + ie is one syllable.
The same sound in a noun: the ending vowel is all that changes.
ei versus ai: the conditional has the e.

blocks.title: Say the pronoun cluster fast
blocks.text: Combined pronouns are said as one unstressed word glued to the verb: [[glielo-DIco]], [[me-la-riPORta]], [[ce-ne-SOno]]. If you give each pronoun its own stress you sound like a grammar book. Say them quickly and softly, then land on the verb. And in the conditional, stress the double consonant: [[poTREBbe]], [[saREBbe]], [[vorREBbero]].

sections.title: Fiducia, cartelli, turisti e reclami
sections.intro: Credit and trust in a small-town shop, the sign and the municipal police, tourists and locals in the South, and the art of complaining so that everyone keeps their dignity.

blocks.text: In Roccamarina a shop runs on [[fiducia]]. The customer who forgot her wallet says [[segna]], and the shopkeeper writes it in a notebook under the counter; Nando's bar has run on that notebook for eighteen years. [[Paghi la prossima volta]] is not a favour, it is the system: the money comes, usually, and the relationship is worth more than the twelve euros. The flip side is that nothing is anonymous. The German tourist is a transaction; Mrs Rizzo is Franca's mother, Nando's cousin's mother-in-law, and the woman who will tell forty people by evening whether the bike was good. A discount is given for who the person is, a repair is done for free when it is your fault, and a refund is almost never asked for because a replacement and an apology are expected instead. Say [[ha ragione]] early and often.

Everything a shop puts on the street is regulated. The [[insegna]] on the wall needs an [[autorizzazione]] from the comune and, above a certain size, a yearly tax; a board on the pavement, a bike on display, two chairs and a pump are [[occupazione di suolo pubblico]] and need a separate permit, paid by the square metre and the day. The [[vigili urbani]] (the municipal police, now officially [[polizia locale]]) enforce it, along with parking, noise after ten, the market stalls and the beach vendors; they are not the carabinieri, they know your name, and the fine for an unauthorised sign starts around a hundred euros. The practical approach is Antonella's: ask before, fill in the form, buy the stamps, and keep the board inside until the paper arrives. Pasquale, as always, will have told you first.

blocks.title: Turisti e paesani
blocks.text: From June to September the Salento fills with Italians from the North, Germans, Dutch, French and, lately, cyclists from everywhere, and the economy of a town like Roccamarina is made in those four months. The locals' attitude is affectionate and practical: tourists pay more (the [[prezzo da turista]] is real but modest), they get served politely in the Lei, and they are forgiven everything except a loud voice at the wrong hour. A tourist who speaks Italian, even badly, even with a Canadian accent, is moved at once to a different category: [[parla italiano!]] and the coffee is offered. Klaus, with his [[potrebbe]] and [[vorrei]], is already half a regular.

Italians complain constantly among themselves and carefully to the person responsible. The polite complaint has a grammar: it starts with [[mi scusi, ma]] or [[senta]], continues in the conditional ([[avrei un problema]], [[ci sarebbe un errore]]), states the fact without accusation ([[la gomma è di nuovo a terra]]), and leaves the other side room to put it right. Raising your voice loses the argument; so does demanding a refund before the shopkeeper has offered a remedy. On the other side, the apology has three parts, in this order: [[ha ragione]] (you're right), [[mi dispiace]] (I'm sorry), [[è colpa mia]] (it's my fault), then the remedy, free. Done well, a complaint ends with a coffee and a customer for life. Done badly, it ends with the whole town knowing within the hour, and the town does not forget.

blocks.title: Il vicino che si lamenta
blocks.text: Every street has a Pasquale: the neighbour who checks your sign, your participles and your permits, and tells you [[da amico]]. He is irritating and indispensable. He knew about the suolo pubblico before you did, he will know when the vigili are coming, and when the comune loses your form he will know whose cousin to call. The correct response to his complaints is to invite him in: [[vorresti entrare?]] He will say [[entrerei]], and stay for an hour.
